headline: Facebook counted anger as five likes

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Stop checking every page
slides.text: Early Facebook meant visiting friends' profiles one by one. **In 2006 News Feed gathered their updates in one place.**

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: A billion people a month
slides.text: Users protested at first, then stayed. **By 2012 more than a billion people used Facebook monthly.**

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Comments, or arguments
slides.statLabel: points for a significant comment vs. a like, Facebook's 2018 scoring
slides.text: In 2018, citing well-being, Facebook began ranking posts by the comments they sparked. **Its researchers found publishers and parties tilting posts toward outrage.**

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Yes, inside Facebook by 2019
slides.text: Facebook's own researchers flagged the effect by 2019. **Outside researchers still argue over how much it mattered.**

slides.label: The cleanup
slides.title: Turning down the dial
slides.text: In September 2020 Facebook cut the angry reaction's weight to zero. **From 2021 it gave political comments and shares less weight.**

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: 3.6 billion people a day on Meta's apps, June 2026
Friends' news in one place, free, since 2006
More than a billion monthly users by October 2012
costs: Publishers and parties tilting posts toward outrage, Facebook's researchers found (WSJ, 2021)
An angry reaction once counted five times a like (Washington Post, 2021)
More uncivil posts in the ranked feed than a plain timeline (Science, 2023)
slides.text: The feed keeps billions of people in touch. **By its makers' own research, it also favored outrage.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: Chasing the wrong number
slides.text: Facebook counted comments as a sign of meaningful talk. But a fight earns comments too, **so the count rose either way.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: Ask what else moves your number
slides.text: A count of replies can't tell a good talk from a fight. **Ask what else moves your number.**
